scenario_text: A fintech startup wants to launch a personal loan app for young professionals. They want quick disbursal, maybe under 10 minutes. The product team is small — 3 people — and the CEO wants to launch an MVP in 2 months, then iterate based on user feedback. Requirements will definitely change as they learn what users want.

requirements.statement: The system shall disburse loans within 10 minutes of approval
requirements.business_justification: Quick disbursal increases customer satisfaction and reduces loan application abandonment
requirements.assumptions: Loan approval process is automated and does not require manual intervention
requirements.acceptance_criteria: Loan disbursal occurs within 10 minutes of approval, as measured by system logs

requirements.statement: The system shall provide a mobile-responsive online loan application portal
requirements.business_justification: Customers expect to apply from mobile devices; mobile-first design increases application completion rates
requirements.assumptions: Users have smartphones with stable internet connectivity
requirements.acceptance_criteria: Portal renders correctly and is fully functional on screen widths from 320px to 1920px
applicable_regulations: Master Direction on Digital Payment Security Controls (RBI/2020-21/74 DoS.CO.CSITE.SEC.No.1852/31.01.015/2020-21) [issued 18 Feb 2021; in force six months from publication]

requirements.statement: The system shall allow for iterative updates and changes based on user feedback
requirements.business_justification: Requirements will change as the product team learns from user feedback; system must accommodate iterative updates
requirements.assumptions: Product team will provide regular feedback and requirements updates
requirements.acceptance_criteria: System allows for seamless updates and changes to existing features without requiring significant rework

requirements.statement: The system shall track the status of loan applications, including pending, approved, and rejected, for both users and administrators.
requirements.business_justification: The CEO wants to launch an MVP in 2 months, then iterate based on user feedback, implying the need for tracking and monitoring loan application status.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: Users can view the status of their loan application on the portal, and administrators can view the status of all loan applications in a centralized dashboard.

requirements.statement: The system shall allow users to cancel their loan applications at any time before approval.
requirements.business_justification: The CEO wants to launch an MVP in 2 months, then iterate based on user feedback, implying the need for flexibility in the loan application process.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: Users can cancel their loan applications on the portal, and the system updates the status accordingly.

requirements.statement: The system shall handle failed checks and unavailable external services, with retries and fallbacks to ensure loan application processing continues.
requirements.business_justification: The system needs to be resilient to external service failures and failed checks to meet the 10-minute disbursal requirement.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: The system retries failed checks and unavailable external services up to 3 times before escalating to administrators for manual intervention.
applicable_regulations: Master Direction on Digital Payment Security Controls §12 (RBI/2020-21/74 DoS.CO.CSITE.SEC.No.1852/31.01.015/2020-21) [issued 18 Feb 2021; in force six months from publication]

requirements.statement: The system shall be configured to allow administrators to set thresholds for loan amounts, interest rates, and repayment terms.
requirements.business_justification: The system needs to be flexible to accommodate changing business requirements and user feedback, implying the need for configurable thresholds.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: Administrators can set and update loan amount, interest rate, and repayment term thresholds on the portal.
applicable_regulations: Master Direction — Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016 §75(d) (RBI/DBR/2015-16/18) [updated 14 Aug 2025]

requirements.statement: The system shall store loan application data, including user information, loan details, and repayment history, for a minimum of 2 years.
requirements.business_justification: The system needs to maintain a record of loan applications and repayments to facilitate iteration based on user feedback and to meet regulatory requirements.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: The system stores loan application data in a secure database for a minimum of 2 years, with regular backups and data archiving.
applicable_regulations: The Aadhaar (Authentication and Offline Verification) Regulations, 2021 §27 (No. 2 of 2021 (K-11020/240/2021/Auth/UIDAI)) [updated 15 Dec 2025]

requirements.statement: The system shall be designed to handle a minimum of 100 concurrent loan applications, with a maximum response time of 5 seconds.
requirements.business_justification: The system needs to meet the 10-minute disbursal requirement, implying the need for high performance and scalability.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: The system can handle a minimum of 100 concurrent loan applications, with a maximum response time of 5 seconds, as measured by load testing.

requirements.statement: The system shall be accessible on mobile devices with screen sizes between 320x480 and 1080x1920 pixels.
requirements.business_justification: The system needs to be mobile-responsive to meet the requirement [REQ-002] The system shall provide a mobile-responsive online loan application portal.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: The system is accessible on mobile devices with screen sizes between 320x480 and 1080x1920 pixels, with a minimum font size of 14pt.

risk_register.title: Early warning signals monitored on credit accounts
risk_register.cause: No requirement covers this obligation. (Master Directions on Fraud Risk Management in Commercial Banks (including RRBs) and AIFIs §3.1 (RBI/2024-25 Fraud Risk Management) [revised 2024])
risk_register.consequence: Regulatory breach found at audit or inspection, with penalty and rework.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall monitor credit accounts against early warning signals and flag accounts showing them for review under the bank's fraud risk framework.

risk_register.title: System clocks synchronised to NIC/NPL time servers
risk_register.cause: No requirement covers this obligation. (CERT-In Directions under section 70B(6) of the IT Act, 2000 — information security practices and reporting of cyber incidents §6(i) (No. 20(3)/2022-CERT-In) [issued 28 Apr 2022])
risk_register.consequence: Regulatory breach found at audit or inspection, with penalty and rework.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall synchronise all its clocks to the NIC or NPL NTP servers (or servers traceable to them), so that log timestamps are reliable.

risk_register.mitigation: Confirm with the stakeholders which statement is correct.

risk_register.title: Small team — key-person dependency
risk_register.cause: The problem statement says: "The product team is small — 3 people — and the CEO wants to launch an MVP in 2 months, then iterate based on user feedback."
risk_register.consequence: Losing one person stalls the project.
risk_register.mitigation: Pair on critical components, document as you go, and identify a backup for each area.
evidence: The product team is small — 3 people — and the CEO wants to launch an MVP in 2 months, then iterate based on user feedback.

risk_register.title: Integrations authenticated, encrypted and rate-limited
risk_register.cause: No requirement provides this control (practice: Industry practice (OWASP API Security Top 10)).
risk_register.consequence: An exploitable weakness reaches production.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: Every integration with an external system shall be mutually authenticated, encrypted in transit, allow-listed and rate-limited, with failures logged.

risk_register.title: Role-based access with least privilege for staff and administrators
risk_register.cause: No requirement provides this control (regulation: Cyber Security Framework in Banks §8.3 (RBI/2015-16/418) [2016 framework (partly superseded by the 2023 IT directions)]).
risk_register.consequence: An exploitable weakness reaches production.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall grant staff access by role on a least-privilege, need-to-know basis, and enforce maker-checker approval for sensitive operations.

risk_register.title: Strong customer authentication — a second factor at login and for high-value actions
risk_register.cause: No requirement provides this control (regulation: Master Direction on Digital Payment Security Controls §34 (RBI/2020-21/74 DoS.CO.CSITE.SEC.No.1852/31.01.015/2020-21) [issued 18 Feb 2021; in force six months from publication]).
risk_register.consequence: An exploitable weakness reaches production.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall authenticate customers with at least two factors at login, and require step-up authentication for transactions above the organisation-approved risk threshold.

risk_register.title: Fixed deadline
risk_register.cause: The problem statement says: "The product team is small — 3 people — and the CEO wants to launch an MVP in 2 months, then iterate based on user feedback."
risk_register.consequence: Scope is cut or quality slips to hold the date.
risk_register.mitigation: Agree what is in the first release, track it weekly, and protect testing time.

risk_register.title: Input validated and secure coding practices applied
risk_register.cause: No requirement provides this control (practice: OWASP ASVS (industry practice; not in the knowledge base)).
risk_register.consequence: An exploitable weakness reaches production.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall validate all input on the server side and be built and tested against the OWASP Application Security Verification Standard.

risk_register.title: Security events monitored and alerted on
risk_register.cause: No requirement provides this control (regulation: Cyber Security Framework in Banks §19.6(b) (RBI/2015-16/418) [2016 framework (partly superseded by the 2023 IT directions)]).
risk_register.consequence: An exploitable weakness reaches production.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall forward security events to the bank's security operations monitoring and raise alerts on anomalous access or activity.

risk_register.title: Sessions time out and repeated failed logins lock the account
risk_register.cause: No requirement provides this control (regulation: Master Direction on Digital Payment Security Controls §53 (RBI/2020-21/74 DoS.CO.CSITE.SEC.No.1852/31.01.015/2020-21) [issued 18 Feb 2021; in force six months from publication]).
risk_register.consequence: An exploitable weakness reaches production.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall end inactive sessions after a defined timeout and temporarily lock access after repeated failed login attempts.

risk_register.title: Vulnerability management, patching and security testing before release
risk_register.cause: No requirement provides this control (regulation: Cyber Security Framework in Banks §7.1 (RBI/2015-16/418) [2016 framework (partly superseded by the 2023 IT directions)]).
risk_register.consequence: An exploitable weakness reaches production.
risk_register.mitigation: Add the requirement: The system shall undergo vulnerability assessment and penetration testing before go-live and after major changes, and its components shall be patched under the bank's patch management policy.
